correctness.rationale: Every canonical root is extreme; exact integer Gram identities make antipodes uniquely distance-squared 8 and all distinct-edge shells {2,6} or {4}, recovering L(G). Whitney's sole triangle/claw ambiguity is resolved by the affine dimension of the six-point component, computed from its centered distance Gram matrix (2 versus 3). Graph isomorphisms induce coordinate-permutation congruence, and metric isometries extend to intrinsic affine isometries. The strict <1 entrywise squared-distance error bound rounds to the unique original even shell. The general argument is rigorous and does not rest on finite tests; the standard-library verifier checked 1694 graph instances.

value.rationale: A complete equivalence classification for canonical Euclidean symmetric-edge polytopes across all graphs is a structural inverse theorem: it sharply refines the known graphic-matroid/unimodular classification, distinguishes every pair of nonisomorphic trees that share a crosspolytope face lattice, resolves Whitney's exceptional ambiguity intrinsically and provides a universal deterministic error margin. These facts concern a natural exact object rather than arbitrary finite recomputation. The classical line-graph lemma is credited.
